strengths: Jointly selecting pipeline partitions and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies addresses a useful infrastructure problem. Experiments with ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge establish concrete relevance to computer vision.

Table 2 reports meaningful measured improvements: on ENVB, UniAP improves throughput over the strongest available baseline by 1.20× for BERT, 1.18× for ViT, and 1.37× for Swin. Matching Galvatron’s throughput on several ENVA workloads while reducing search time is also valuable.

The evaluation covers five Transformer models and multiple hardware configurations, with throughput measurements, search times, ablations, and prediction-error analysis. The reported 3.59% average throughput-estimation error provides encouraging evidence for the cost model on the selected strategies.

The workflow, pseudocode, hardware specifications, solver settings, and topology-aware BERT case study make the approach reasonably understandable. Source: :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-rjs4y9ne/call-bc937af9c9ef48189bb12cdf9f694a83/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The principal concern is a substantive correctness gap in the stated optimization. Equations (6a–c) ensure contiguity within stages but do not enforce their topological order. For a two-layer graph u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and contiguity constraints, yet Equation (4) assigns zero communication cost to their edge. Thus, the optimizer can favor placements whose transfers are omitted from its objective. Appendix A proves contiguity only and does not resolve this issue.

GPipe activation-memory accounting is incomplete as documented. Algorithm 1 constructs M using micro-batch size b=B/c, and Equation (5) sums these costs once, although the illustrated GPipe schedule retains activations from all c micro-batches before backward propagation. The missing accumulation factor or equivalent accounting could change feasibility and strategy selection. No measured peak-memory validation establishes the claimed OOM guarantee.

The solver-ready formulation is insufficiently specified. Equations (3) and (4) contain fourth-degree products of placement and strategy variables, such as PuiPviSukSvl, rather than only quadratic terms. An auxiliary-variable reformulation is possible, but none is supplied. This omission may be straightforward to repair, yet it prevents reproducing the claimed MIQP directly from the manuscript.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix D permits termination after 60 seconds or after 15 seconds with a gap below 4%, without reporting achieved gaps or exact small-instance comparisons. Consequently, the experiments do not establish globally optimal solutions even for the estimated objective. Treating solver runtime as a fixed timeout also does not establish the complexity of obtaining an optimum; the limited scaling experiment cannot validate that claim.

The experiments do not isolate the central claim that joint optimization improves upon hierarchical optimization. Figure 7 compares joint search with inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only search, which establishes the usefulness of combining parallelism types. A comparison against hierarchical search using identical costs, candidate strategies, and execution infrastructure is absent. Hierarchical decomposition alone does not imply a smaller feasible space or suboptimality, and the reported gains also involve differences in cost-model accuracy and implementation.

Search-time improvements require narrower interpretation. The reported metric measures UOP and excludes profiling, while the paper attributes substantial speedups to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baseline searches. CPU-resource controls and timing breakdowns are insufficient to separate algorithmic improvements from these implementation differences. These limitations qualify the efficiency claims; the unresolved formulation and feasibility issues are what primarily determine the weak-reject recommendation.
